programs.name: normray
programs.purpose: Trace dynamic rays from locations on an interface in a triangulated sloth model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: NORMRAY - dynamic ray tracing for normal incidence rays in a sloth model

params.name: surface
params.description: Shoot from the surface when set.

params.name: nonsurface
params.description: Include rays that do not reach the surface when set.

params.name: nangle
params.description: Number of angles per source; the selfdoc says 101.

params.name: nxz
params.description: Samples per ray in the optional ray file.

params.name: nt
params.description: Samples per ray in the optional wave file.

params.name: krecord
params.description: Interface index used to select output rays.

params.name: prim
params.description: Select direct or single-reflected rays; requires krecord and refseq.

params.name: ffreq
params.description: Fresnel frequency; positive values open the Fresnel file.

params.name: fresnelfile
params.description: Binary Fresnel output file when ffreq is positive.

params.name: refseq
params.description: Repeatable interface index followed by reflection, transmission, or stop sequence.

params.name: fangle
params.description: Listed in the selfdoc but never read; the first angle is computed from interface angle, nangle, dangle, and ashift.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Dynamic ray tracing uses iterative triangle crossings, float calculations and transcendental functions. RayEnd is written as a native C struct. XInterface and ZInterface, and AInterface when surface=0, are opened and read without checking success. For nrays=1, as[i]=180 uses i before initialization, causing undefined behavior; only the final source's ray ends are written to stdout.
programs.difficulty_reason: Dynamic ray tracing has complex state, reflection sequences and more than 1500 lines.

test_cases.description: Trace rays from a generated interface; the source program also creates the required interface files.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 xedge=0,1 zedge=0.5,0.5 sedge=1,1 kedge=1 sfill=0.2,0.2,0,0,1,0,0 sfill=0.2,0.8,0,0,1,0,0 normray=1 normface=0 nrays=2 > model.bin && normray nrays=2 nangle=3 dangle=10 surface=0 outparfile=norm.out < model.bin > rays.bin

test_cases.description: Trace surface rays with an optional wave file.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 xedge=0,1 zedge=0.5,0.5 sedge=1,1 kedge=1 sfill=0.2,0.2,0,0,1,0,0 sfill=0.2,0.8,0,0,1,0,0 normray=1 normface=0 nrays=2 > model.bin && normray nrays=2 surface=1 nangle=3 dangle=15 nt=16 wavefile=wave.bin outparfile=norm.out < model.bin > rays.bin

programs.name: tri2uni
programs.purpose: Sample a triangulated sloth model on a uniform rectangular grid.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRI2UNI - convert a TRIangulated model to UNIformly sampled model

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of samples in the fast, depth dimension.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of samples in the horizontal dimension.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Float coordinate accumulation, boundary snapping and linear sloth evaluation can differ with rounding and compiler contraction.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program locates each sample in a triangulated model and interpolates sloth.

test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 | tri2uni n1=5 n2=5 d1=0.25 d2=0.25 > sloth.bin

test_cases.description: Sample a gradient over an interior subgrid.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 | tri2uni n1=3 n2=3 d1=0.25 d2=0.25 f1=0.25 f2=0.25 > sloth.bin

programs.name: trimodel
programs.purpose: Build a triangulated sloth model from boundaries and region properties.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRIMODEL - make a triangulated sloth (1/velocity^2) model

params.name: maxangle
params.description: Maximum smoothing angle in degrees; the selfdoc says 5.0.

params.name: normray
params.description: Generate interface files for normray when 1.

params.name: normface
params.description: Interface set used for normal-ray source locations.

params.name: xedge
params.description: Repeatable edge x coordinates; each occurrence requires matching zedge and sedge arrays.

params.name: kedge
params.description: Edge indices; omitted trailing indices are zero.

params.name: sfill
params.description: Repeatable seven-value region sloth specification: x,z,x0,z0,s00,dsdx,dsdz.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Spline smoothing and triangulation depend on floating-point geometry, transcendental functions and insertion order. Native model serialization is platform dependent.
programs.difficulty_reason: Model construction combines spline smoothing, constrained triangulation and region filling.

test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 > model.bin

test_cases.description: Build a two-region model with a labeled interface and physical properties.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 xedge=0,0.5,1 zedge=0.5,0.6,0.5 sedge=1,1,1 kedge=1 maxangle=3 sfill=0.2,0.2,0,0,1,0,0 sfill=0.2,0.8,0,0,0.5,0,0 densfill=0.2,0.8,2 qfill=0.2,0.8,100 > model.bin

programs.name: triray
programs.purpose: Trace dynamic rays through a triangulated sloth model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRIRAY - dynamic RAY tracing for a TRIangulated sloth model

params.name: nxz
params.description: Samples per ray in the optional ray file.

params.name: nt
params.description: Samples per ray in the optional wave file.

params.name: prim
params.description: Select direct or single-reflected rays; requires krecord and refseq.

params.name: fresnelfile
params.description: Fresnel output file when ffreq is positive.

params.name: refseq
params.description: Repeatable interface index followed by reflection, transmission, or stop sequence.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Dynamic ray tracing uses iterative triangle crossings, float arithmetic and transcendental functions; RayEnd records are native C structs with platform-dependent layout.
programs.difficulty_reason: Dynamic ray tracing has complex reflection and transmission state and exceeds 1500 lines.

test_cases.description: Trace a small fan of direct rays.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 | triray xs=0.5 zs=0 nangle=5 fangle=-30 langle=30 outparfile=ray.par > rays.bin

test_cases.description: Trace rays with a reflecting interface and optional ray and wave files.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 xedge=0,1 zedge=0.5,0.5 sedge=1,1 kedge=1 sfill=0.2,0.2,0,0,1,0,0 sfill=0.2,0.8,0,0,1,0,0 | triray xs=0.5 zs=0 nangle=5 fangle=-20 langle=20 refseq=1,1 krecord=1 prim=1 nxz=16 nt=16 rayfile=paths.bin wavefile=waves.bin outparfile=ray.par > rays.bin

programs.name: triseis
programs.purpose: Generate Gaussian-beam synthetic seismograms from a triangulated sloth model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRISEIS - Gaussian beam synthetic seismograms for a sloth model

params.name: zs
params.description: Source surface z coordinates, matching xs.

params.name: zg
params.description: Receiver surface z coordinates, matching xg.

params.name: ds
params.description: Source spacing; zero makes the location routine span the surface.

params.name: fs
params.description: First source position along its surface.

params.name: dg
params.description: Receiver spacing; zero makes the location routine span the surface.

params.name: fg
params.description: First receiver position along its surface.

params.name: reftrans
params.description: Enable complex reflection and transmission coefficients.

params.name: aperture
params.description: Receiver aperture; a supplied value is transformed with asin(aperture*PI/180).

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Ray tracing, cubic interpolation, complex Gaussian-beam accumulation and FFTs are sensitive to operation order, float rounding and transcendental implementations. Output is raw floats, not SU traces.
programs.difficulty_reason: Gaussian-beam synthesis combines dynamic ray tracing, complex amplitudes, interpolation and FFTs.

test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 | triseis xs=0.2,0.8 zs=0,0 xg=0.2,0.8 zg=1,1 ns=1 ng=5 nt=128 dt=0.01 nangle=9 fangle=-30 langle=30 krecord=1 > seis.bin

trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 xedge=0,1 zedge=0.5,0.5 sedge=1,1 kedge=1 sfill=0.2,0.2,0,0,1,0,0 sfill=0.2,0.8,0,0,1,0,0 qfill=0.2,0.2,100 | triseis xs=0.2,0.8 zs=0,0 xg=0.2,0.8 zg=0,0 ns=1 ng=5 nt=128 dt=0.01 nangle=9 kreflect=1 krecord=1 prim=1 atten=1 reftrans=1 > seis.bin

programs.name: uni2tri
programs.purpose: Approximate a uniformly sampled sloth grid with a triangulated model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UNI2TRI - convert UNIformly sampled model to a TRIangulated model

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of samples in the fast dimension.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of samples in the second dimension.

params.name: mm
params.description: Intermediate model output interval; nonpositive values become zero.

params.name: tol
params.description: Vertex closeness criterion in samples for method 3.

params.name: sfill
params.description: Repeatable seven-value region sloth specification: x,z,x0,z0,s00,dsdx,dsdz.

params.name: ifile
params.description: Optional initial triangulated model, read inside the selected method.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Iterative maximum-error selection and vertex insertion depend on float rounding, interpolation, sorting and triangulation geometry. Native model serialization is platform dependent.
programs.difficulty_reason: Three iterative adaptive triangulation methods maintain complex geometric state.

test_cases.description: Convert a sampled model with single-vertex insertion.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 | tri2uni n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 > sloth.bin && uni2tri n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 method=1 errmax=0.01 verbose=0 < sloth.bin > model.bin

test_cases.description: Use an initial model and the multi-vertex method.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 > initial.bin && tri2uni n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 < initial.bin > sloth.bin && uni2tri n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 ifile=initial.bin method=2 errmax=0.01 verbose=0 < sloth.bin > model.bin

test_cases.description: Use the spacing-controlled method with a region fill.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 | tri2uni n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 > sloth.bin && uni2tri n1=9 n2=9 d1=0.125 d2=0.125 method=3 tol=2 errmax=0.01 verbose=0 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 < sloth.bin > model.bin
